title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Approving the Henan High People's Court to Carry Out the Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases
keywords_en: administrative litigation; High People's Court handling administrative cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Official Reply Approving the Henan High People's Court's Pilot Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases

Fa [2019] No. 158

Henan High People's Court:

Your court's "Request for Instructions on Adjusting the Jurisdiction Scope of the Two-Level Railway Transport Courts over Trans-Administrative Region Cases" (Yu Gao Fa [2019] No. 10) has been received. Upon deliberation, in accordance with the provisions of Article 18, paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the spirit of the "Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on the Centralized Jurisdiction of People's Courts over Administrative Cases across Administrative Regions" (Fa Fa [2015] No. 8), we approve your request in principle.

The reform shall be advanced under the unified leadership and coordination of the local Party committee, in accordance with the spirit of the central institutional reform and the requirements of institutional reform in the region. When refining the implementation plan, the administrative adjudication functions of basic people's courts at all levels shall be retained to maintain the integrity of the litigation system and to serve local law-based administration. Intermediate people's courts may select one or two basic people's courts with a high volume of cases, strong adjudication capabilities, a favorable judicial environment, and convenient transportation as central courts to implement centralized jurisdiction. The plaintiff's right of choice shall be fully respected; the plaintiff may choose either the court of the defendant's domicile or the central court to have jurisdiction. Local courts and the centralized jurisdiction courts shall strengthen communication and coordination, balance the separation of mediation and adjudication as well as the combination of mediation and adjudication, and jointly work to coordinate and resolve administrative disputes. Where railway courts are used to centrally administer jurisdiction over some administrative cases, specific issues such as the transfer of backbone administrative adjudication personnel must be properly resolved first to avoid a decline in the quality of administrative adjudication, and future reform directions for railway courts and the centralized jurisdiction of other types of cases shall also be considered. A unified mechanism for adjudication standards shall be established to prevent inconsistencies in adjudication standards for similar cases due to different courts having jurisdiction. Before the implementation of the "Plan," a public announcement shall be made. Your court shall strengthen research and guidance, and promptly report any new situations and issues arising during implementation to the Supreme People's Court.
